prompt: Write part of a deposition transcript (about 400 words) of a plaintiff in a car accident lawsuit. The defense lawyer asks (lines start with 'Q:') and the plaintiff answers (lines start with 'A:'). Accident: rear-end collision in Baytown, Texas. Injury: concussion. Ask about the accident, treatment and daily life. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1403; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather not give my full name on the record yet. You can refer to me as the plaintiff.

Q: Fair enough. Where were you living at the time of the collision?
A: I was living in Baytown, Texas, in the same house I'd been renting for a few years.

Q: Let's talk about the day of the accident. Where were you headed?
A: I was driving to the grocery store on the main road near my neighborhood. It was late afternoon and traffic was moderate.

Q: Describe what happened.
A: I had stopped at a red light. The next thing I remember is a loud bang and my head snapping forward and then back against the headrest. The car behind me had hit me from the rear.

Q: Did you lose consciousness?
A: I don't think I fully lost consciousness, but everything went fuzzy for a moment. I remember the airbag going off and ringing in my ears.

Q: Did you seek medical attention that day?
A: Yes. An ambulance took me to the emergency room. They did a scan and told me I had a concussion.

Q: What symptoms have you experienced since then?
A: Headaches almost every day, and bright light bothers my eyes. I get dizzy when I stand up too fast. I also have trouble concentrating on long conversations and reading, so I've had to take breaks at work.

Q: Have you received follow-up treatment?
A: Yes, I've seen my primary care doctor several times and a neurologist. I was told to rest and avoid screens for stretches of time. I also went to physical therapy for my neck, which was sore after the impact.

Q: How has this affected your daily life?
A: I used to run three mornings a week. I haven't been able to do that since the accident because the headaches flare up. I've also been more irritable, and my family has noticed. I've had to cut back on social plans because noise and crowds are hard for me to handle.

Q: Have you missed time from work?
A: Yes, I took several days off early on, and I've been working reduced hours since I returned. My supervisor has been understanding, but I'm not performing at the level I used to.

Q: Before the accident, did you have any prior head injuries or neurological conditions?
A: No, nothing like that. I had never been treated for a head injury before this.
